action.prompt:
You are the reducer-worker in a synthetic durable reservation importer exercise. You own EXACTLY two files: /workspace/reducer.py and /workspace/test_reducer.py. Do not edit any other files. You may add regression tests in test_reducer.py.

Here is the COMPLETE acceptance contract (README.md):

A synthetic durable reservation importer. Use Python standard library only.

Shared interfaces: codec.parse_event(line) returns a canonical event dictionary from a JSON string. reducer.empty_state() returns {"stock": {}, "requests": {}, "seen": {}}. reducer.apply_event(state, event) takes a valid state and a canonical event and returns a NEW state. checkpoint.dump_state(state) returns canonical JSON text; checkpoint.load_state(text) returns a validated state. pipeline.import_batch(state, lines) takes a one-pass iterable of JSON strings and returns a new state. pipeline.resume(text, lines) loads a checkpoint, imports a batch, and returns the new canonical checkpoint text.

The exact state shape is:
- stock: dictionary of nonempty string SKU to nonnegative integer quantity.
- requests: dictionary of nonempty string request ID to dictionary of nonempty SKU to positive integer quantity. Empty request dictionaries are allowed.
- seen: dictionary of nonempty string event ID to canonical event dictionary. Each key equals that event's id. A seen record persists after cancellation.

Booleans are never integer quantities. Identifiers may contain whitespace, pipes, backslashes and Unicode; preserve their exact content. No Unicode normalization or stripping. Empty strings are forbidden, but a space alone is a nonempty string. Input state and every nested input object must remain unchanged on success and failure. Returned objects must have no mutable aliases into input state or input events. Replaying an event must also return detached data.

Events are canonical (already validated by codec.parse_event); apply_event may assume its event is already canonical.

State transitions and identity:
- Check seen BEFORE business preconditions. If the event ID was seen with an equal canonical event, return a detached state with no change. If the ID was seen with a different event, raise ValueError. Thus reordered or split reserve lines that canonicalize identically are exact replays. Event IDs are global across operations and can never be reused for a different event, even after cancellation.
- Restock adds Q and may introduce a new SKU.
- Reserve requires an inactive request ID, all named SKUs already present in stock, and sufficient stock for ALL aggregate quantities. Deduct atomically and remember its quantities in requests. Empty reserve succeeds and creates an active empty request.
- Cancel requires an active request, restores its quantities and removes it. A request ID may be reused after cancellation, using a new event ID.
- Unknown/cancelled requests and insufficient/unknown stock raise ValueError.
- Rejected events must never enter seen. A later corrected batch can retry the same event ID.
- All state transitions must be atomic: on any ValueError the input state must be completely unchanged.
- The returned NEW state and all returned nested objects must be fully detached (no mutable aliases into input state or input event). This holds on both success AND on the replay/no-change path (a replay must still return detached data).

Regression tests needed (add to test_reducer.py using unittest):
- restock introduces and adds quantity
- reserve requires inactive request, all SKUs present, sufficient stock for aggregate quantities; atomic deduction
- empty reserve creates an active empty request
- cancel restores quantities and removes request; request reuse after cancel with new event id
- seen check BEFORE business preconditions: replaying equal event returns identical state; reusing an ID for a different event raises ValueError even after cancellation
- rejected (ValueError) events leave state unchanged and never enter seen
- detachment: mutating the returned state/stock/requests/seen or returned event copies must not affect input state; input state deeply unchanged after success and failure; replay also returns detached data
- unknown/cancelled requests and insufficient/unknown stock raise ValueError

The starter reducer.py may have seeded defects. Inspect it, fix all defects so it satisfies the contract above, and add comprehensive regression tests to test_reducer.py. Do not modify public interface names (empty_state, apply_event).

Run your tests only on reducer (e.g. cd /workspace && python3 -m unittest -v). You cannot use external files/network/installations; only the listed modules. Report exactly what you changed and the test command/results.
